# SPE Round 5 plan: invoice extraction, OCR cleanup skip on two-column layouts

Round 4 missed on config R. The stop streak is 0 of 3. This round tests one fix for F9 and keeps everything else fixed.

Defaults I chose:
- The last requirement ID from round 4 is not in front of me. I label new rows N1 to N6 here and renumber them to follow the spec.md sequence when I write the file.
- Each trial count, model pin, and grader stays the same as round 4 unless this plan names a change.

## 1. Specify

### Proposals from round 4

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1. Keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopted | F9 is the only new failure. The fix changes one thing compared with R, so the eval can tie any difference to the skip rule. |
| P2. Add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Rejected for this round (default) | No config is at a ceiling. Q measured 0.93 and R measured 0.88, so the current 60 invoices still separate the configs. New invoices also need reference fields from the AP lead, and only the user can arrange that. Adding them now would also break comparison with round 4. This is logged as D-r05-1. |
| P3. Drop config P | Adopted (default) | P trails Q on every metric in round 4. Dropping P frees budget for config S. Q becomes the reference config. The user can bring P back next round. |

### Requirement table (round 5)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | Config S runs OCR cleanup on every invoice except those the layout check marks as two-column. On those it passes the raw text to the extractor. | P1, r04 F9 | `check_cleanup_skipped` reads the tool-call log per trial |
| N2 | The layout check decides two-column from the PDF text positions only. It never reads reference fields. | r04 F9, leak rule | Leak scan of trial transcripts, plus code review of the check |
| N3 | The layout check marks every invoice listed under F9 "Seen in" as two-column and marks no single-column invoice as two-column. | r04 F9 | Gate 3b: `check_layout_detector` against the F9 list |
| N4 | On two-column invoices, S extracts every line item that the AP lead's reference lists. | r04 F9 | `check_line_items` on the two-column slice |
| N5 | On scanned invoices, S keeps R's total accuracy. The skip rule must not undo the cleanup gain that R's Why claimed. | r04 "Which Why broke" | `check_total` on the scanned slice |
| N6 | Config P is retired. Its round 1 to 4 rows stay in the log with a note. | P3 | None. This is a scope row. |

| ID | Question | Option A | Option B | Work affected | Decides | Status |

| D-r05-1 | Add 15 scanned handwritten invoices to the eval set? | Add them in round 6 as a separate slice with AP lead references | Do not add them | Task set, cost, comparison with earlier rounds | The user, with the AP lead for references | Open. Default for r05 is not added. |

## 2. Predict

Configs: Q (reference) = Sonnet 5.5 with the schema-first prompt. R = Q plus OCR cleanup as a tool. S = R plus the two-column skip rule. Each config changes one thing compared with the one before it.

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | Grader check | Q | R | S | Same as last round | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 invoices | `check_fields` (vendor normalized, invoice number exact, date parsed equal, line items matched, total to the cent) | 0.93 ± 0.02 | 0.88 ± 0.02 | 0.94 ± 0.03 | Q 0.93, R 0.88, S none | Q and R have not changed, so they repeat round 4. S removes the F9 loss and keeps a small gain on scanned totals. |
| Line-item recall, two-column slice | `check_line_items` | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.70 ± 0.08 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | Filled from the gate 2 regrade | On two-column invoices S passes the same raw text that Q sees, so S should match Q. R drops line items here per F9. |
| Total accuracy, scanned slice | `check_total` | 0.85 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | Filled from the gate 2 regrade | Scanned invoices are mostly single-column, so S runs cleanup on them just as R does. |

The slice numbers are estimates. Gate 2 measures the round 4 slice values. If a round 4 value falls outside the band I gave above, I will move that prediction with a stated reason and save it before launch. I will not change any number after the first trial runs.

The naive guess for every cell is the round 4 value. In round 4 the naive guess beat my prediction for R. This round shows whether my predictions add anything over that guess.

## 3. Evaluate

### After approval, in this order

1. Save the user's prompt ("go again") and this session's planning answers word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Add the round 5 table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Add D-r05-1 and D-r05-2 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit locally as `spe(r05): specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` with round 5, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs Q, R, S, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` I leave `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit locally as `spe(r05): predict`.
3. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 5`. No prompt text contains a typed round number.

### Gates before launch

| Gate | Pass condition | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Grader selftest | The oracle passes `check_fields`, `check_line_items`, `check_total`, and `check_cleanup_skipped`. Empty output fails and wrong output fails. | Halt and report. The grader is broken. |
| 2. Regrade of round 4 as control | The regrade gives exactly Q 0.93 and R 0.88 field accuracy. It also records the slice values for the round 4 rows. | Halt and report a grader bug. It becomes a failure entry, with the original and regraded numbers side by side. |
| 3a. Dry run | 3 cells run end to end: S on one F9 two-column invoice, S on one scanned invoice, and Q on one plain invoice. Each output passes its schema. | Fix the harness and rerun the dry run. |
| 3b. Layout detector check | The detector marks every F9 invoice as two-column and marks no single-column invoice. | Halt. S would not test P1. |

Then I commit the harness locally as `spe(r05): evaluate` and launch the Workflow.

### Workflow arguments

- `ROUND`: 5
- `configs`: Q, R, S
- `model`: Sonnet 5.5, pinned as in round 4
- `tasks`: the same 60 invoices with the AP lead's reference fields
- `trials_per_cell`: same as round 4
- `split_cell_extra_trials`: up to 2 more per split cell, capped at 60 extra trials in total
- `budget_cap`: 1.25 times the actual round 4 spend. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped, and each skip is logged.
- Trials get a JSON schema. Code checks run first. A judge is used only for vendor-name matches that the normalizer cannot settle.
- Trials cannot read the graders, the reference fields, or the predictions. A transcript scan voids any trial that peeked.
- The run ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

Round 4 ran 3 configs (P, Q, R). Round 5 also runs 3 configs (Q, R, S). The trials and tasks are the same, so I expect the spend to be close to round 4's. The extra split-cell trials can add up to the 1.25 times cap.

### Close-out, when the completion notice arrives

- Add the round 5 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md` with the verdicts and the closer of prediction or naive guess. Under them, write "Which Why broke" for each miss.
- Set F9's fix to the measured result. Add any new failure types as F10 and up.
- Add a "Proposed for round 6" table to spec.md. Write `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Commit locally as `spe(r05): learn` and tag it `spe-r05`.
- I will not push anything.

### Halt conditions

I will halt and report if the budget cap is hit, if an answer key leaks, if a grader breaks, or if a decision needs the user. D-r05-1 does not block this round.
